cells.tense: Present tense — here, with the pen.
cells.verb: holding two growing things in care at once
cells.place: where you keep adjusting the mix
cells.ask: offer one piece of this tending into the open where someone can see it — and let the release that follows completion be fulfillment, not defeat
cells.core:
You're carrying two living demands at once and keeping both fed. Not choosing between them and not forcing either — adding here, subtracting there, feeling for what each one needs. That is the work, and you're in it without making a show of it.

The care you're giving has form. It isn't vague goodwill; it's the structure you keep rebuilding so what's growing can keep growing. When you get it right, nobody sees the adjustment — they just see something thriving.
cells.sheetLine: You keep two living things fed without forcing either.

cells.tense: Future tense — bracing at a future that can't be written in.
cells.verb: gripping the outcome harder than the tending
cells.place: ahead of where the thing actually is
cells.ask: let one thing you're tending come to you at its own pace, and let the vision that comes be one you could actually live inside — dreaming from what you've already been through, not from what you're afraid of
cells.core:
You're already living in the version where it worked — and you're managing everything backward from there. Every check, every adjustment, every preemptive fix is aimed at an outcome that hasn't happened yet. The tending has turned into steering, and the steering has turned into holding on.

You can feel it in your hands. What was care has a grip in it now. The thing you're growing can feel the difference, even if you can't name when it changed.
cells.sheetLine: You're managing forward from an ending that hasn't arrived.

cells.tense: Past tense — still standing at a door that's already behind you.
cells.verb: withholding the care that used to come naturally
cells.ask: follow one star you already chose, past the point where it got hard — the radiance comes when what you've been cultivating reaches completion, not when you decide to start again
cells.core:
There was a time you tended something well and it didn't hold — or it held and you lost it anyway. Since then the care has been there but the reaching has stopped. You know how to keep things alive; you've just stepped back from actually doing it.

The adjusting you do now is maintenance, not cultivation. You're keeping the shape of it without the growth inside. The door is behind you, and the reach hasn't come back.
cells.sheetLine: You know how to tend, and you've stopped reaching.

cells.tense: Disowned present — pen down in a room you're already writing.
cells.verb: already tending, calling it something else
cells.ask: name one adjustment you made this week as the care it was — let someone see the intent behind it, and let the release come from that being enough
cells.core:
You're already doing the steady, unglamorous work of keeping two things in balance — feeling for the right moment to add, to pull back, to change the mix. You do this every day. You just describe it as problem-solving, or logistics, or just getting through the week.

The care is real and it's shaping what grows around you. But the one person who can't see it is you. You've been calling your tending a series of practical decisions, and the tending has been the point all along.
cells.sheetLine: The care is already working. You call it getting through the week.

flags.detail: "a while ago" — a cell knows no one's past
